_comment: Declarative manifest of INSTALLABLE (dynamic) vessels — the single source of truth for vessel-ctl.sh install/uninstall. Built-in vessels are baked into the image; this file is for vessels added/removed at runtime (federation, future). Each vessel: name (== systemd unit name), workdir (run dir; supports $REPO_ROOT), exec (bun entrypoint, relative to workdir), env (STATIC literal Environment= lines), secrets (keys from secrets.env.sh that must be in /etc/substrate/env — supplied to the unit via EnvironmentFile, NOT Environment=), restart, health_port (for /health + self-recovery), self_recovery (add to self-recovery-tick VESSELS), post_install (optional shell run after start, e.g. capture a dynamic relay multiaddr into /etc/substrate/env).

vessels.name: metric-collector-vessel
vessels.description: Substrate-authored sample collector (metricSample shapes; lift empirical test).

vessels.name: human-surface-vessel
vessels.description: Human-facing surface vessel — the UI a human resolver talks to; the only vessel a UI-only federated spoke needs to serve locally.
vessels._host_comment: HOST is 0.0.0.0 because this vessel exists to be reached by a human from OUTSIDE the container. THE REASON THIS WORKS IS NOT LINE ORDER, and the previous wording here had the systemd rule backwards. render-unit.sh does emit these env lines after EnvironmentFile=/etc/substrate/env, but that buys nothing: systemd.exec states plainly that settings from EnvironmentFile= override settings made with Environment=, regardless of which line comes first. Line order decides only FILE-vs-FILE precedence (a later EnvironmentFile beats an earlier one — which is why /etc/substrate/env is now listed last, after .substrate-secrets). So if /etc/substrate/env ever carried a HOST= line, it would win and this 0.0.0.0 would be silently ignored. The bind holds only because gen-env.sh never emits HOST, PORT or VESSEL_ID into /etc/substrate/env — an accident of that file's contents, not a guarantee of this file's position. Anyone adding HOST/PORT/VESSEL_ID to gen-env's env heredoc breaks every vessel's Environment= bind at once. A 127.0.0.1 bind does not accept the DNAT'd traffic a `docker run -p` publish delivers from the container's bridge IP, so the host port mapping exists and is dead — the vessel answers /health in-container and nothing on the host. stateful-ui-vessel, which this vessel replaces, sets 0.0.0.0 for the same reason. Registration is unaffected: the discovery payload uses SELF_ENDPOINT = http://127.0.0.1:$PORT (src/config.ts), a constant independent of HOST.
vessels._post_install_comment: SKIPS THE BUILD WHEN dist CAME FROM GIT, and that guard is load-bearing. ui/dist is now TRACKED, because the substrate updates itself by pulling and nothing rebuilds on pull — git is the delivery channel. A rebuild does not reproduce the committed bundle byte-for-byte (vite content-hashes, and the container's bun differs from the operator's: the same source produced CN--oDvm, Y3nhnr7c, CIgDXFb9 and aOP5YrJ- on four machines), so building over a tracked dist leaves MODIFIED tracked files, `git pull --ff-only` then refuses, and the vessel silently stops converging to origin/dev. That is the same wedge that stranded the hub's development-vessel 124 commits behind. Build ONLY when dist is absent — a fork building from a tree that predates the tracked bundle, or a source-only checkout. vessel-ctl runs `bun install` ONLY in the rendered WorkingDirectory (the server), never a build. Paths are LITERAL: post_install is handed to the container shell verbatim, so $REPO_ROOT/$RUNTIME are NOT expanded here (federation-relay's hook is literal for the same reason). HOME and the bun cache dir are pinned OUTSIDE the repo: a HOME redirected into the tree leaked a 146MB bun cache into it. vessel-ctl SWALLOWS this hook's stdout, stderr AND exit status (`csh "$post" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`), so the hook writes its own log and a terminal OK/FAILED sentinel — that log is the only evidence a build failed, and callers should assert ui/dist exists rather than trust the install's ok:true.
vessels.post_install: L=/workspace/human-surface-ui-build.log; D=/workspace/git/super-repo/repos/human-surface-vessel/ui/dist; if [ -f "$D/index.html" ]; then echo "UI_BUILD_SKIPPED (dist came from git — rebuilding would dirty tracked files and wedge pull-sync)" > "$L"; else { export HOME=/root; export BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR=/root/.bun/install/cache; set -x; cd /workspace/git/super-repo/repos/human-surface-vessel/ui && /root/.bun/bin/bun install && /root/.bun/bin/bun run build && test -d dist; } > "$L" 2>&1 && echo UI_BUILD_OK >> "$L" || echo UI_BUILD_FAILED >> "$L"; fi

vessels.name: federation-relay
vessels.description: Public libp2p Circuit Relay v2 — the from-anywhere reachability anchor.
vessels.post_install: for i in $(seq 1 20); do m=$(grep -m1 'RELAY_MULTIADDR=' /workspace/fed-relay.log 2>/dev/null | sed 's/RELAY_MULTIADDR=//'); [ -n "$m" ] && { grep -v '^RELAY_MULTIADDR=' /etc/substrate/env > /etc/substrate/env.tmp && mv /etc/substrate/env.tmp /etc/substrate/env; echo "RELAY_MULTIADDR=$m" >> /etc/substrate/env; echo "captured RELAY_MULTIADDR=$m"; break; }; sleep 1; done

vessels.name: federation-transport-vessel
vessels.description: libp2p reachability + cross-substrate resolve-over-http + /health sensing surface.
vessels._workdir_comment: REVERTED TO $REPO_ROOT ON 2026-09-16 AFTER THE FALSIFIER FAILED — the note below is kept because the diagnosis is correct and the blocker is now known. Repointing this to the image copy put the transport in a crash loop with 'Cannot find module @avigopal/libp2p-federation-transport'. REASON: the image's vendored dep is a STUB. In the image, node_modules/@avigopal/libp2p-federation-transport is a real directory containing only three symlinks (bun.lock, package.json, node_modules) pointing into /vessels/libp2p-federation-transport, with no src/ and no build output, so bun cannot resolve the module. In the working clone the same dep is a real directory with full contents (LICENSE, README, .d.ts files — an actually installed package). The Dockerfile copies package.json, src and tsconfig into /vessels/libp2p-federation-transport and runs bun install there, then rewrites federation-relay's dep to that file: path and installs again — which produces the stub. MAKING THE TRANSPORT IMAGE-RESIDENT THEREFORE REQUIRES COMPLETING THE VENDORED PACKAGE IN THE IMAGE, not just repointing this line. Tracked as a gap. THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS, UNCHANGED: this manifest entry is the site that actually decides, because the baked unit in /usr/lib/systemd/system is shadowed by the one vessel-ctl RENDERS into /etc/systemd/system from here — fixing the unit file alone changed nothing. The baked unit in /usr/lib/systemd/system is shadowed by the one vessel-ctl RENDERS into /etc/systemd/system from this manifest entry, so fixing the unit file alone changed nothing; measured on a stock container, the rendered unit still carried the clone path. Three failures came from running out of /workspace/git/super-repo, all measured: (1) entrypoint enables this unit before the clone exists, so install reports 'WORKDIR ABSENT — dependencies NOT installed' and a healthy-looking container federates with nobody; (2) pull_cutover stashes local changes there, silently reverting a deployed transport fix mid-session; (3) the federation probe shares that directory and a branch checkout once left HEAD where the file does not exist, disabling the verifier by the routine activity of the thing it verifies. The image already bakes this whole directory WITH node_modules installed (see the federation-relay block in Dockerfile.substrate, which vendors @avigopal/libp2p-federation-transport to a file: path and runs bun install at build time), so nothing new ships — this points at what was already built and never used. THE TRADE, STATED: the transport can no longer be self-modified at runtime through the clone; a substrate-authored change to it needs an image rebuild. That is deliberate for a vessel whose job is reachability — it must not be able to break its own delivery path — but it is a real loss of self-modification and the honest follow-up is to mirror it into /vessels like every other vessel rather than leaving it image-only.
